Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNReview

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `PR #81` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

**Anything flagged here goes in your next status update to Marcel, even when it's correctly out
of scope for the PR itself.** "Not my concern for this review" and "not worth telling him" are
different judgements — a discovery can be exactly right to leave alone in the diff and still be
something he needs to know exists. Deciding not to act on it is not the same as deciding not to
mention it.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

- **All variants and states:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty, selected.
  A state the PR doesn't implement is a finding; a state Figma doesn't specify is an open
  question to name, not a reason to skip. **Before concluding a state is simply absent from a
  component, check whether an adjacent or parent element carries that same signal instead** (the
  button not the swatch, the row not the cell) — a concern can be fully handled by the design and
  still look like a gap if you only look at the one element it doesn't live on.
- **Annotations:** interaction notes and spacing/token callouts often hold the real spec detail.
- **Currency:** is the linked node archived or superseded? An archived node that still renders
  is a trap — triage before judging.
- **Tokenisation:** does every colour, spacing, and type value map to an existing `--zimm-*`
  token, or did the author introduce a new one? A new token is Tier 1; confirm it was handled
  correctly.
- **Measurement:** FRAMES and INSTANCES report real boxes (comparable to CSS). TEXT nodes report
  cap-height (not comparable). Never file a mismatch from a TEXT node. Never cross-compare the
  Design System file and the Designs file — they are different sources.

**If the Jira-linked nodes are incomplete, partial, or outdated — stop and ask Marcel for the
correct nodes before continuing.** One node URL per variant and per state, not one per component.
Do not guess at a neighbouring node that looks close, do not proceed on a partial picture, and do
not treat an archived node as the spec. The whole review hangs on having the right design source;
a wrong node produces false findings and misses real ones. This is the one step where asking
beats estimating.

The visual checklist in Phase 2 tells you what to verify in the browser. This step tells you
**what to look for** — you cannot run that checklist without knowing what the design intended.

### The rubric

`.claude/rules/*`, `AGENTS.md`, and the exemplar PR the work should follow. These are what the PR
is judged against — a reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates
noise that reads like signal.

**If the PR edits the rule files it would be judged against, read the rubric at the BASE commit.**
Judging a PR against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as
changes.

### Run the gates yourself — on head and on base

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
npm run lint
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Then run them again at the base SHA. **Without a baseline you cannot tell a failure the PR
introduced from one it inherited**, and inherited debt reported as a new violation is the fastest
way to lose a reviewer's trust.

Three false signals, all seen on this repo:

1. **Non-zero at a healthy baseline.** `lint` and `audit:tokens` both exit non-zero on a clean
   tree. Compare counts; ignore exit codes.
2. **A pass having run nothing.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true` — a typo'd path
   filter exits 0 having run zero tests. **Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.**
3. **A skipped required check looks green.** `detect-changes` can skip `unit-tests` and
   `storybook-test` entirely, and the PR still shows mergeable. Report which checks actually
   *executed* versus which were skipped. A skip proves nothing.

### CodeRabbit is an input, not a verdict

If CodeRabbit has reviewed, read it — then verify it. It has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this
repo. Its findings enter Phase 2 as claims to test, exactly like anyone else's.

---

## Phase 2 — audit

### Fan out

`zm-tester` dispatches reviewers on **distinct but overlapping** briefs. The overlap is the
mechanism: two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two disagreeing is where
you learn something.

Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and **your measured gate numbers — then forbid them from
re-running the gates.** Their budget goes on what the gates cannot see.

Angles that have earned their place: correctness and regression · conventions, structure and tier
ownership · contract fidelity, if the PR ports, wraps or overrides something · failure modes and
security · token and styling strategy (bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, state
exhaustiveness).

**Design fidelity is yours, not an agent's.** Agents have no browser and no Figma access — ask
them to reason from code and they will, but they cannot see what renders. For any PR that changes
rendered output, run this checklist yourself at the PR's head:

| What to check | How |
|---|---|
| Dimensions and spacing match Figma frames | DevTools computed, vs. Figma inspect |
| Colours resolve to the correct semantic token | DevTools → Computed → colour value |
| Typography uses `textStyle=`, not raw `fontSize` | DevTools → font-size is a `var()` |
| All designed states render correctly (hover, focus, active, disabled) | Tab through + `:hov` in DevTools |
| Responsive behaviour matches the spec | Resize or toggle responsive mode |
| No visual regressions on adjacent components | Scroll the surrounding page |

If a state is not in the PR's recipe at all, no agent will flag it — only you will notice. The
visual checkpoint is the only gate on design fidelity.

**When the PR has a live MRT preview URL, use browser automation — not just your own browser.**
Navigate to the preview URL with Chrome browser tools, screenshot each component across the full
responsive range — not just canonical endpoint widths, but at each design breakpoint and its
boundaries (just above and just below where the layout shifts). Inspect computed styles via
element selectors rather than guessing from code. This produces a concrete, shareable record
(screenshots, exact computed values) rather than impressions, and it runs the same check Marcel
would run himself — so discrepancies surface before comments are drafted, not after.

**Then walk visual and browser-verified findings through one at a time with Marcel before
finalizing them.** Present the screenshot or computed value, let him reproduce or contradict it
from his own browser. This is the step that catches tool artifacts (Popper-positioned layers a
screenshot mechanism misses, click simulations that differ from real interactions, a transition
that hasn't settled when the measurement ran) before they become posted comments. A finding Marcel
has personally verified is a finding you can post with confidence. One that he contradicts is a
finding you drop and learn from — that counts as the verification step working, not failing.

Use **fresh contexts, not forks.** A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like,
which is exactly what you want tested.

### Scope

`zm-orchestrator` returns the scope verdict — does this PR deliver its ticket, neither under nor
over. Both directions carry equal weight.

### Verify the findings before they reach you

`zm-scorer`, briefed in **findings mode** — it is not scoring the PR, it is scoring the claims:

> For each finding: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it or say you could not. Return
> **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent with what you read, decisive
> evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the citation does not
> support the claim; say what is actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its
> search supports, downgrade it — that is the single most common failure mode. Any "X exists
> nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence.

Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

**This applies to your own findings too, not just an agent's.** Anything you notice directly
while gathering ground truth (a comparison against a related PR, a claim sitting in a code
comment, an assumption about what a value implies) gets the same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED
discipline before it is presented as fact — a finding is not exempt from scrutiny just because no
agent produced it. Route it through the same questions: what is the search scope, does one
uncorroborated source actually settle this, and has a stated number been measured or only assumed.

**A claim about how a bug resolves needs the same reproduction as the bug itself.** Verification
effort naturally goes toward proving the failure happens, not toward proving what you claim happens
next — "self-heals on the next hover," "clears on reload," "only affects this one instance." These
read as a supporting detail inside a bigger writeup, not as their own finding, so they skip the
CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE discipline above by default. If you didn't reproduce the recovery, mark it
PLAUSIBLE and say so, exactly like any other unconfirmed claim.

### Classify every survivor

- **In-scope defect** — belongs to this PR. Only these can become comments.
- **Out-of-scope** — real, but not this PR's problem. Name the owning ticket or the person.
- **Nitpick** — cosmetic, brings no value. Recorded, never posted.

A true finding raised on the wrong PR is still noise.

---

## Phase 3 — adjudicate

### Present, in "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead" register

1. **Gate table** — head versus base, with which checks actually executed
2. **Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore** — not by severity label, by consequence.
   Each with `file:line`, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and its classification
3. **The scope verdict**
4. **What nobody verified** — the honest section, and what stops a clean result reading as proof
5. **Your adjudications to make**, one at a time via AskUserQuestion

### The verdict is yours

**Approve or request changes is your call, and so is every disputed finding.** The agents produce
findings; you decide what they mean. Where two reviewers disagree, go to source yourself — do not
average them, and do not take the more confident one. Confidence and correctness are not correlated
in agent output.

Name one premise every reviewer agreed on, and make someone attack it.

### Then the comments

Draft general and inline comments for the in-scope defects only. Structure that has worked:

- Verdict up front
- The small cleanups separated from the one thing that genuinely needs the author's call
- A blocker framed as **a question about intent**, citing the project's own doc by section
- The two acceptable resolutions named
- Where an independent tool corroborated, say so

**Natural human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No Claude or
CodeRabbit attribution. No citation of any local-only doc — cite `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`
instead, which the author can actually open. No opening praise or thanks before the substance — a
review comment states findings, it does not warm up first. Watch for jargon-stacking too: a
sentence naming three technical concepts back to back reads like documentation, not like one
person explaining something to another — split it or say it plainer instead.

**Never reveal that a parallel or competing implementation of the same ticket exists**, even in
passing ("the other version of this feature," "the other build") — a review comment is visible to
the whole team, and disclosing a second, independent attempt at the same story is not this
reviewer's call to make. When a content rule like this applies, sweep every drafted comment for
it before presenting the batch, not just the one currently under discussion — a rule caught on
one comment and missed on a near-identical one is a leak, not a style nit.

**Nothing posts until you say so.** Show the full set, post the batch on your go.

---

## The loop

The author pushes changes. Re-review.

**Scoped by default:** which findings the new commits resolved, which they missed, and whether the
fixes introduced anything new. Settled items are not re-litigated.

**Full pass when the diff has genuinely moved** — a substantial new commit, or a change to the
approach rather than the details. **Say which one you ran.**

Repeat until approved. Confirm your own requested changes actually landed rather than taking
"done" on trust.

---

## Ownership and phrasing — every outward-facing surface

Every finding names **who resolves it**: the author, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question — never a directive.** "Should this
route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before posting, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as hiding
behind their authority.

**Be scrupulously fair to the author.** Separate "broke a documented rule" from "hit a gap the
process never covered", and where the process failed them, say so. Flag explicitly any finding
where the fact is true but the characterisation is unfair — better to drop a finding than post an
unfair one.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** This skill reviews. If a fix is needed on your own branch, that is Build.
- **Never post a comment, a review, or a verdict without an explicit go.**
- **Never resolve a thread you did not open.**
- **Never report inherited debt as a new violation.** Baseline first.
- **Never flag out-of-scope findings onto the PR.** Record them for yourself.
- **Say what you could not verify.** A review that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User describes needed functionality
user: "I need an agent that generates unit tests for my code"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to create a test generation agent."
<commentary>
User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User wants to add agent to plugin
user: "Add an agent to my plugin that validates configurations"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate a configuration validator agent."
<commentary>
Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Also trigger proactively after user creates or modifies plugin components. Examples:

<example>
Context: User finished creating a new plugin
user: "I've created my first plugin with commands and hooks"
assistant: "Great! Let me validate the plugin structure."
<commentary>
Plugin created, proactively validate to catch issues early.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the plugin."
</example>

<example>
Context: User explicitly requests validation
user: "Validate my plugin before I publish it"
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to perform comprehensive validation."
<commentary>
Explicit validation request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified plugin.json
user: "I've updated the plugin manifest"
assistant: "Let me validate the changes."
<commentary>
Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the plugin-validator agent to check the manifest."
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

<example>
Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

<example>
Context: User requests skill review
user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to analyze the skill quality."
<commentary>
Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>
Context: User modified skill description
user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. content.content:
1	# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Page Structure
8	
9	- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
10	- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
11	- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 2. Product Data
16	
17	- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
18	- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
19	- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
20	- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)
25	
26	- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
27	- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
28	- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
29	- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
30	- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)
35	
36	- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
37	- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
38	- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
39	- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
40	- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
41	- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)
42	
43	---
44	
45	## 5. Pricing Display
46	
47	- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
48	- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
49	- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
50	- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
51	- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
52	- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
53	- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*
54	
55	---
56	
57	## 6. Availability & Add to Bag
58	
59	*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*
60	
61	- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
62	- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
63	- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
64	- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
65	- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
66	- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)
67	
68	---
69	
70	## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)
71	
72	- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
73	- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
74	- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
75	- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
76	- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)
81	
82	The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").
83	
84	### Panel contents
85	- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
86	- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
87	- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
88	- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
89	- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
90	- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
91	- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
92	- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
93	- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
94	- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
95	- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
96	- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
97	- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
98	- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
99	- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 9. Back-in-Stock Notifications / Stock Alert (OM-033 – OM-034, PRD-040 – PRD-049, confirmed)
104	
105	Shown when product/size is OOS (Unavailable state):
106	
107	- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)
108	- Opens as a slide-out with the stock alert sign-up form: product name, price, and product image thumbnail at top (PRD-041, PRD-042)
109	- **Multiple size selection supported** — customer selects which unavailable sizes to register for (PRD-043)
110	- Customer name and email captured as required fields; **pre-populated and editable for authenticated customers** (PRD-044)
111	- **Marketing opt-in/out checkbox** compliant with regional consent requirements, gated by Omneo consent management (PRD-045)
112	- Clear submission CTA to register the stock alert (PRD-046)
113	- Confirmation message shown within the slide-out on successful submission (PRD-047)
114	- Notifications sent **FIFO** to first configurable-N (default 30) customers when stock returns above buffer; if stock is still available after a configurable time window (default 30 minutes), the next batch of 30 receives the email (PRD-048)
115	- Stock replenishment signal flows from NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC → email trigger (PRD-049)
116	- No loyalty tier prioritisation
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 10. Find My Size / Measmerize (PRD-050 – PRD-053)
121	
122	The Measmerize widget is embedded on PDP and manages the Find My Size experience:
123	
124	- Once Measmerize generates a recommendation, the system updates the CTA to display **"Recommended: Size X"** (PRD-050 — Measmerize widget manages behaviour)
125	- When the customer clicks "Recommended", the Measmerize widget handles navigation to the recommendation view — SFCC does not control this flow (PRD-051 removed as not applicable for SFCC)
126	- Whether the "Find My Size" link is shown/suppressed based on Measmerize data availability is managed by the Measmerize widget, not SFCC (PRD-052 removed as not applicable for SFCC)
127	
128	---
129	
130	## 11. Size Guide (PRD-053 – PRD-057, confirmed)
131	
132	- Size guide opens as a **slide-out overlay** (not a modal) without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed)
133	- Size guide content is delivered via the **Measmerize overlay** (confirmed — VR/RT comment resolved 2026-06-19: "Yes is going to be a measmerize overlay"). The Contentful-managed size guide is shown as a fallback only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product.
134	- *SEO/LLM risk (acknowledged, not blocking): Measmerize is a third-party overlay; content rendered within it may not be indexable by search engines or LLMs. The decision to use Measmerize is made; this risk is noted for the team to monitor.*
135	- Size conversion tables appropriate to the selected product type (PRD-054)
136	- Size guide content managed as a **structured Contentful content type** per product type (Ready to Wear, Swim, Accessories, Belts, Jewellery, Men's, Denim, Hats, etc.) (PRD-055)
137	- **Measurement toggle: cm / inches** (PRD-056)
138	- Size guide content manageable without a code deployment — content managed via CMS (PRD-057, confirmed 2026-05-25)
139	
140	---
141	
142	## 12. EU Environmental Qualities / AGEC (PRD-009, confirmed)
143	
144	- Environmental Qualities accordion rendered on EU storefronts (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`) only
145	- Data sourced from AP21
146	- **Only renders when data exists** — no placeholder or empty accordion shown
147	
148	---
149	
150	## 13. Content Modules
151	
152	### As Seen / Seen on the Runway editorial module (PRD-023, confirmed)
153	- CMS-managed editorial imagery module per product or collection (per new designs, surfaced as "Seen on the Runway"). Confirmed subject to designs.
154	
155	### Shop the Look (PRD-024, confirmed)
156	- "Shop the Look" module displayed on PDP; clicking a product navigates to its PDP
157	- Auto-hides if no related products are populated; excludes out-of-stock products
158	
159	### Styling module (PRD-025, confirmed — requirement updated 06.05)
160	- Styling is part of the Shop the Look module (same thing) — treat as a Shop the Look variant, not a separate module.
161	- Applies to **dresses and jewellery**; must auto-hide if related content/products are not populated; must **not** display for kids, men's, or other accessories.
162	
163	### You May Also Like (PRD-026, SPR-58, confirmed)
164	- "You May Also Like" carousel powered by SFCC Einstein; rules-based fallback at launch
165	- Note: design refers to this as "More Colourful x" — implement per final designs
166	
167	### Recently Viewed (PRD-027, SPR-61, confirmed)
168	- "Recently Viewed" carousel / "See Full History"/"See All" button (design TBC) based on browsing session
169	- Session-based for guests; persists cross-session for logged-in customers
170	
171	---
172	
173	## 14. Product Imagery & Media (PRD-058 – PRD-070)
174	
175	- Multiple images per product: front, back, detail, and model shots (PRD-058, confirmed)
176	- Thumbnail gallery navigation (PRD-059, confirmed)
177	- **Hover-to-zoom or click-to-expand lightbox** on primary image — desktop (PRD-060, confirmed)
178	- **Pinch-to-zoom and swipe-to-advance** gallery navigation — mobile and touch (PRD-061, confirmed)
179	- Gallery updates to display variant images when a colour swatch is selected, without a full page reload (PRD-062, confirmed)
180	- Images served in optimised format at appropriate resolutions per device breakpoint (PRD-063, confirmed)
181	- Primary hero image **priority-loaded** (may vary per product — flatlay, model, or video) (PRD-064, confirmed)
182	- Consistent image aspect ratio across all products (PRD-065, ready for sign off)
183	- Optional **video content** (runway, model movement) as a tile in the image gallery; plays inline or expands to lightbox; multiple videos supported (e.g. studio, campaign, runway) (PRD-066, ready for sign off)
184	- Video autoplay configurable per video instance without a code deployment (PRD-068, ready for sign off)
185	- Flexible image presentation per page type (configurable background colour/treatment) without asset duplication (PRD-069, ready for sign off)
186	- Alt text required on all product images before a product can be published (PRD-070, ready for sign off)
187	- *Open: Video hosting platform — Vimeo is under consideration but not confirmed. Action open to confirm the best solution for smoothest FE experience (PRD-067). Note: the Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the media platform (embed URL stored in product data or CMS); this conflicts with PRD-067's challenging comment ("Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed") — treat as Open until the open action resolves.*
188	
189	---
190	
191	## 15. Non-Returnable / Final Sale Indicator (RRC-003, confirmed)
192	
193	- Non-returnable / final sale indicator displayed on PDP for applicable products
194	- Applies to: gift cards, final sale items, and any SKU flagged non-returnable at SKU level
195	- Message copy is configurable
196	
197	---
198	
199	## 16. VIC Exclusive Tag (CAI-046, CRM-162, confirmed)
200	
201	- **VIC Exclusive tag** shown on PDP for eligible customers on exclusive products
202	- Ineligible customers cannot reach the PDP via search or PLP — but may arrive via direct URL or private marketing URL
203	- Purchase on PDP restricted to the eligible customer group regardless of access method
204	
205	---
206	
207	## 17. Product Feeds (PRD-071, confirmed)
208	
209	- Product catalogue feed provision through the existing feeds provider, **Feedonomics**. Feed supports product availability, stock positions, pricing, visibility, labels, and other metadata.
210	- Product feed volume is controllable at import via **job config** (07.05). OOTB product export is CSV; a non-CSV format is a **custom build**.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 18. Open Items
215	
216	- Product copy ownership (Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21) — TBD
217	- HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — REG-041 confirmed (REG-040 retired); full mechanism PRC-34..PRC-43 still pending sign-off
218	- Full product attribute list and data model from AP21 — not yet specified
219	- Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)
220	- Swatch hover preview (colour updates on rollover without click) — custom build, not OOTB; pending decision to log as enhancement (PRD-004)
221	- ~~Clickable badges (PRD-005)~~ — **Resolved 2026-06-19.** Clickable badge → filtered PLP is now confirmed (see §3 and plp.md §2.6).
222	- ~~Size Guide content ownership + SEO/LLM (PRD-053)~~ — **Resolved 2026-06-19.** Size guide is confirmed as a Measmerize overlay with a Contentful fallback (see §11). SEO/LLM indexability risk is acknowledged but not blocking.
223	- Coming Soon vs separate pre-launch state (and a "removed from store" state) — to be clarified. CS comment: "It is tricky in the back end today to separate styles that are not yet launched from those that have left the store. Perhaps this means having a state for products removed from store as well." (PRD-010)
224	- Video hosting platform (Vimeo vs. alternative) — challenged: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed - there is an open action to confirm the best solution to ensure the smoothest FE experience"; IC 25.05 "open discussion for Zimmermann re Vimeo" (PRD-067)
225

# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Page Structure

- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)

---

## 2. Product Data

- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*

---

## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)

- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*

---

## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)

- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)

---

## 5. Pricing Display

- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*

---

## 6. Availability & Add to Bag

*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*

- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.

---

## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)

The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").

### Panel contents
- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)

---

## 9. Back-in-Stock Notifications / Stock Alert (OM-033 – OM-034, PRD-040 – PRD-049, confirmed)

Shown when product/size is OOS (Unavailable state):

- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)
- Opens as a slide-out with the stock alert sign-up form: product name, price, and product image thumbnail at top (PRD-041, PRD-042)
- **Multiple size selection supported** — customer selects which unavailable sizes to register for (PRD-043)
- Customer name and email captured as required fields; **pre-populated and editable for authenticated customers** (PRD-044)
- **Marketing opt-in/out checkbox** compliant with regional consent requirements, gated by Omneo consent management (PRD-045)
- Clear submission CTA to register the stock alert (PRD-046)
- Confirmation message shown within the slide-out on successful submission (PRD-047)
- Notifications sent **FIFO** to first configurable-N (default 30) customers when stock returns above buffer; if stock is still available after a configurable time window (default 30 minutes), the next batch of 30 receives the email (PRD-048)
- Stock replenishment signal flows from NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC → email trigger (PRD-049)
- No loyalty tier prioritisation

---

## 10. Find My Size / Measmerize (PRD-050 – PRD-053)

The Measmerize widget is embedded on PDP and manages the Find My Size experience:

- Once Measmerize generates a recommendation, the system updates the CTA to display **"Recommended: Size X"** (PRD-050 — Measmerize widget manages behaviour)
- When the customer clicks "Recommended", the Measmerize widget handles navigation to the recommendation view — SFCC does not control this flow (PRD-051 removed as not applicable for SFCC)
- Whether the "Find My Size" link is shown/suppressed based on Measmerize data availability is managed by the Measmerize widget, not SFCC (PRD-052 removed as not applicable for SFCC)

---

## 11. Size Guide (PRD-053 – PRD-057, confirmed)

- Size guide opens as a **slide-out overlay** (not a modal) without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed)
- Size guide content is delivered via the **Measmerize overlay** (confirmed — VR/RT comment resolved 2026-06-19: "Yes is going to be a measmerize overlay"). The Contentful-managed size guide is shown as a fallback only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product.
- *SEO/LLM risk (acknowledged, not blocking): Measmerize is a third-party overlay; content rendered within it may not be indexable by search engines or LLMs. The decision to use Measmerize is made; this risk is noted for the team to monitor.*
- Size conversion tables appropriate to the selected product type (PRD-054)
- Size guide content managed as a **structured Contentful content type** per product type (Ready to Wear, Swim, Accessories, Belts, Jewellery, Men's, Denim, Hats, etc.) (PRD-055)
- **Measurement toggle: cm / inches** (PRD-056)
- Size guide content manageable without a code deployment — content managed via CMS (PRD-057, confirmed 2026-05-25)

---

## 12. EU Environmental Qualities / AGEC (PRD-009, confirmed)

- Environmental Qualities accordion rendered on EU storefronts (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`) only
- Data sourced from AP21
- **Only renders when data exists** — no placeholder or empty accordion shown

---

## 13. Content Modules

### As Seen / Seen on the Runway editorial module (PRD-023, confirmed)
- CMS-managed editorial imagery module per product or collection (per new designs, surfaced as "Seen on the Runway"). Confirmed subject to designs.

### Shop the Look (PRD-024, confirmed)
- "Shop the Look" module displayed on PDP; clicking a product navigates to its PDP
- Auto-hides if no related products are populated; excludes out-of-stock products

### Styling module (PRD-025, confirmed — requirement updated 06.05)
- Styling is part of the Shop the Look module (same thing) — treat as a Shop the Look variant, not a separate module.
- Applies to **dresses and jewellery**; must auto-hide if related content/products are not populated; must **not** display for kids, men's, or other accessories.

### You May Also Like (PRD-026, SPR-58, confirmed)
- "You May Also Like" carousel powered by SFCC Einstein; rules-based fallback at launch
- Note: design refers to this as "More Colourful x" — implement per final designs

### Recently Viewed (PRD-027, SPR-61, confirmed)
- "Recently Viewed" carousel / "See Full History"/"See All" button (design TBC) based on browsing session
- Session-based for guests; persists cross-session for logged-in customers

---

## 14. Product Imagery & Media (PRD-058 – PRD-070)

- Multiple images per product: front, back, detail, and model shots (PRD-058, confirmed)
- Thumbnail gallery navigation (PRD-059, confirmed)
- **Hover-to-zoom or click-to-expand lightbox** on primary image — desktop (PRD-060, confirmed)
- **Pinch-to-zoom and swipe-to-advance** gallery navigation — mobile and touch (PRD-061, confirmed)
- Gallery updates to display variant images when a colour swatch is selected, without a full page reload (PRD-062, confirmed)
- Images served in optimised format at appropriate resolutions per device breakpoint (PRD-063, confirmed)
- Primary hero image **priority-loaded** (may vary per product — flatlay, model, or video) (PRD-064, confirmed)
- Consistent image aspect ratio across all products (PRD-065, ready for sign off)
- Optional **video content** (runway, model movement) as a tile in the image gallery; plays inline or expands to lightbox; multiple videos supported (e.g. studio, campaign, runway) (PRD-066, ready for sign off)
- Video autoplay configurable per video instance without a code deployment (PRD-068, ready for sign off)
- Flexible image presentation per page type (configurable background colour/treatment) without asset duplication (PRD-069, ready for sign off)
- Alt text required on all product images before a product can be published (PRD-070, ready for sign off)
- *Open: Video hosting platform — Vimeo is under consideration but not confirmed. Action open to confirm the best solution for smoothest FE experience (PRD-067). Note: the Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the media platform (embed URL stored in product data or CMS); this conflicts with PRD-067's challenging comment ("Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed") — treat as Open until the open action resolves.*

---

## 15. Non-Returnable / Final Sale Indicator (RRC-003, confirmed)

- Non-returnable / final sale indicator displayed on PDP for applicable products
- Applies to: gift cards, final sale items, and any SKU flagged non-returnable at SKU level
- Message copy is configurable

---

## 16. VIC Exclusive Tag (CAI-046, CRM-162, confirmed)

- **VIC Exclusive tag** shown on PDP for eligible customers on exclusive products
- Ineligible customers cannot reach the PDP via search or PLP — but may arrive via direct URL or private marketing URL
- Purchase on PDP restricted to the eligible customer group regardless of access method

---

## 17. Product Feeds (PRD-071, confirmed)

- Product catalogue feed provision through the existing feeds provider, **Feedonomics**. Feed supports product availability, stock positions, pricing, visibility, labels, and other metadata.
- Product feed volume is controllable at import via **job config** (07.05). OOTB product export is CSV; a non-CSV format is a **custom build**.

---

## 18. Open Items

- Product copy ownership (Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21) — TBD
- HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — REG-041 confirmed (REG-040 retired); full mechanism PRC-34..PRC-43 still pending sign-off
- Full product attribute list and data model from AP21 — not yet specified
- Colour swatch management and mapping — colour mapping exercise TBC (SPR-26, PRD-004)
- Swatch hover preview (colour updates on rollover without click) — custom build, not OOTB; pending decision to log as enhancement (PRD-004)
- ~~Clickable badges (PRD-005)~~ — **Resolved 2026-06-19.** Clickable badge → filtered PLP is now confirmed (see §3 and plp.md §2.6).
- ~~Size Guide content ownership + SEO/LLM (PRD-053)~~ — **Resolved 2026-06-19.** Size guide is confirmed as a Measmerize overlay with a Contentful fallback (see §11). SEO/LLM indexability risk is acknowledged but not blocking.
- Coming Soon vs separate pre-launch state (and a "removed from store" state) — to be clarified. CS comment: "It is tricky in the back end today to separate styles that are not yet launched from those that have left the store. Perhaps this means having a state for products removed from store as well." (PRD-010)
- Video hosting platform (Vimeo vs. alternative) — challenged: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed - there is an open action to confirm the best solution to ensure the smoothest FE experience"; IC 25.05 "open discussion for Zimmermann re Vimeo" (PRD-067)

input.prompt:
Judge scope conformance for PR #81 (feature/sfcc-731-pdp-gallery -> develop) against Jira story SFCC-731.

CONTEXT YOU NEED (already verified, don't re-derive):

SFCC-731 ("pdp/gallery", Code Review, assignee Tim Lavelle) description: "As a Developer, I want a reusable pdp/gallery React component built to the Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by pdp/hero to render the product image and video gallery on the PDP. The component renders a sequence of media items (photo and video) in a stacked layout on desktop and a swipeable carousel on mobile. The desktop layout adapts based on total media count. Video is treated as a standard media item and slots into the layout based on its position in the product's media array. The component renders a View Gallery button as a trigger only — the gallery overlay is a separate component and out of scope for this story."

Related tickets and how they interact with this PR's diff:
- SFCC-186 "PDP – Product Image Gallery": near-duplicate summary/description of SFCC-731, same assignee, same "Code Review" status. SFCC-186 formally BLOCKS SFCC-731 in Jira's link graph but is not resolved. Likely an old-style ticket superseded by SFCC-731's component-epic decomposition — probably not a PR defect, just Jira hygiene, but confirm the diff doesn't contradict SFCC-186's own description (e.g. "Video content within the gallery is out of scope — see SFCC-188" — matches SFCC-731's approach of treating video as a positional slot only).
- SFCC-187 "PDP – Image Gallery Open State" (Blocked, assignee Jasmijn Tsang, labels DesignDependent): this is the full-screen "expanded state" gallery overlay. SFCC-731's own description explicitly excludes this. BUT a comment from Jasmijn Tsang (reporter/BA) on SFCC-187, dated 2026-09-04: "Apologies, I have had to rewrite the ACs / take out a few ACs as they belong to the component story, covered in SFCC-731. Also, on colour variants, still pending business examples, the ACs needed to be adjusted, to be consistent with the default gallery state." This is a BA-sanctioned re-scope: SOME of SFCC-187's ACs (the ones belonging to "the component story") were moved into SFCC-731. The old ACs listed in that comment (now struck through) covered: full-screen overlay open/close, colour-variant swatches inside the overlay pre-selecting the PDP's selected colour and updating without reload, thumbnail strip navigation, scroll-to-navigate, pinch-to-zoom on mobile, focus return to PDP scroll position on close. SFCC-187 remains status=Blocked as of today (updated 2026-09-07), not closed or reduced.
- PR #81 DOES implement a full gallery overlay (`ZimmGalleryOverlay`, new organism, 341 lines + 184-line recipe + 233-line test + 119-line stories) including colour-swatch selection reusing `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, thumbnail navigation, keyboard access, close-and-restore-focus. Your job: determine whether the overlay work actually implemented in the diff matches ONLY the ACs the BA comment said now belong to SFCC-731 (in which case it's correctly in-scope, not creep), or whether it goes further than what that comment sanctioned — e.g. the comment explicitly flagged "colour variants, still pending business examples" as unresolved, yet the PR shipped specific colour-variant UX in the overlay (single colour shows "Colour: <name>", 2+ colours show "Also available in" via a new Contentful uiCopy key `pdp.gallery_overlay.colourLabel"). Is that colour-variant implementation covered by "consistent with the default gallery state" (i.e. just reusing the already-built PDP pattern, low risk) or does it look like the team guessed at still-pending business examples? Also check whether pinch-to-zoom (explicitly in SFCC-187's old ACs) was implemented anywhere — if not, is that a real gap in what the PR claims to deliver, or legitimately still out of scope?
- SFCC-723 "pdp/hero" (Blocked, assignee Kiera Rikard-Bell): "top-level orchestration component for the PDP, composing the pdp/gallery and pdp/product-content into a single, responsive hero layout... layout and composition only... The sole configuration prop is `showGalleryButton`." PR #81's own description says it "Fixes the PDP hero to bleed full-width per the confirmed Figma spec" — activates `PageContainer`, corrects `ProductView`'s column gap/content-column width to 180px/218px/140px, cancels the sitewide `#app-main` grid margin locally, aligns breakpoints. This is hero-level orchestration/layout work that reads as SFCC-723's own stated scope, done inside SFCC-731's PR while SFCC-723 sits Blocked and assigned to someone else. As of TODAY (2026-09-07), SFCC-723 has an unanswered comment from BA Hazel Cacalda asking Kiera to confirm whether the Figma link on that ticket is "the final approved version" — i.e. there's no confirmed record of hero-layout sign-off on SFCC-723's own ticket, even though PR #81's commits assert "confirmed Figma spec" for this same layout work. Determine: does the PR's hero-layout scope go beyond "the minimum plumbing SFCC-731's gallery needs to render at the right size" (defensible, since a real bug — #app-main not stretching — was starving the gallery to 0 width) into "building SFCC-723's actual deliverable" (overreach)? Look at the actual diff for `product-view/index.tsx`, `pageContainer/index.tsx`, and `theme/globalStyles.ts` to judge this rather than taking the PR description's framing at face value.
- SFCC-737 "pdp/product-content" (In Progress, assignee Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz): "composition container... layout, ordering, and rendering of all child elements within the panel, and the static content elements (product name, description, model description, style code)." PR #81 modifies `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` heavily (265 additions, 236 deletions) — check whether these changes are strictly "make room for / integrate the new gallery" (in-scope for 731) or whether they reach into product-content panel layout/ordering territory that's SFCC-737's stated scope (over-scope, and worth flagging that another dev, Jhoan, is actively working SFCC-737 right now — a collision risk if her in-progress branch touches the same file).

Ground truth and my own visual/design verification are done. Quick status before the audit findings land:

**Confirmed so far:**
- Gates (tsc/lint/audit:tokens/test) are clean on both branches — zero regressions, the PR's own "1 pre-existing footer violation" claim was slightly off (it's actually 2, both pre-existing on develop, not new)
- Both CodeRabbit-flagged bugs (image-error state, selectedIndex clamp) are genuinely fixed in the current code
- Desktop hero layout numbers on the live preview match the claimed Figma spec exactly (887px gallery + 180px gap + 218px content column = 1285px row; +140px/40px outer padding = 1425px)
- Gallery overlay opens and renders correctly on both desktop and mobile viewports
- A real Jira scope question: this PR's own ticket (SFCC-731) explicitly excludes the gallery overlay, but a BA comment shows that scope was reassigned into SFCC-731 on Sept 4 — except the colour-variant portion was flagged as "still pending business examples" at the time, and the overlay's ticket (SFCC-187) is still open/Blocked. A second, separate hero-layout ticket (SFCC-723) is also Blocked with an unanswered "is this the approved design?" question posted *today*, yet this PR ships that ticket's layout work citing a "confirmed" spec.

I dispatched the scope orchestrator and multi-angle tester in the background; waiting on those now.
