<result>## Scope verdict: PR #81 (feature/sfcc-731-pdp-gallery → develop) vs SFCC-731

Verified against the real diff (`4cdfb47f..HEAD`, checked out at the worktrees, 34 files / +3281/-475), not the PR's own commit-message framing. Where a raw diff stat looked alarming, I re-diffed with `--ignore-all-space` to separate real logic changes from re-indentation noise.

### Territory map — clean

- **SFCC-186** (near-duplicate ticket): no contradiction. Video is still positional-only (`zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:72-73`: *"No real playback source yet... ready for SFCC-188 to wire a real `<video>`/Vimeo source behind"*).
- **SFCC-708** (related-colour swatches): correctly reused, not duplicated — both `product-view/index.tsx` and `product-detail/index.tsx` import `buildRelatedSwatches` from the existing `productInfo.ts`, no reimplementation.
- **SFCC-188** (video in gallery): correctly deferred, matches its Blocked status.
- **SFCC-737** (`pdp/product-content`): **not actually touched.** `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` shows 501 changed lines in `git diff`, but `git diff --ignore-all-space` collapses that to ~40 real lines: a new `PageContainer` import/wrap (two calls, `boxed={false}` for the hero, `boxed={true}` for recommendations), an `H1` content change, and a constant rename. The rest is pure re-indent from the new wrapper element. No reordering of name/description/model-info/style-code, no accordion changes. The suspected collision with Jhoan's in-progress SFCC-737 branch does not materialize in this diff.
- **SFCC-91 `ui-kits` atoms** (`zimmButton`, `zimmColourSwatch`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup`): additive, backward-compatible extensions only (`variant?: 'square'|'circle'`, `appendColon?`, `sx?` passthrough) — existing `square`/PDP styling is preserved byte-for-byte inside a new conditional branch, not altered. Legitimate reuse to support the overlay, not a rewrite.
- `.claude/registry/*.md` — mechanical auto-regen churn, not a finding, per instructions.
- No Tier 1 file touched anywhere in the 34-file list.

### Finding 1 — OVER-delivery into SFCC-723 ("pdp/hero") territory — HIGH confidence

SFCC-723 is Blocked, assigned to Kiera Rikard-Bell, and its own BA (Hazel Cacalda) has an **unanswered** question on the ticket asking whether its Figma link is even final. Despite that, this PR implements SFCC-723's literal job description — *"composing the pdp/gallery and pdp/product-content into a single, responsive hero layout"* — with Figma node IDs cited directly in the code:

- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:771` — `// SFCC-731 — 140px right / 40px bottom, per Figma "pdp/hero" (node 7932:45339).` applied to `ProductView`'s outer wrapper.
- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:798` — `// SFCC-731 — 180px gap between gallery/content at lg+, 32px stacked below.`
- `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:860-890` — the content column pinned to a fixed `width={['100%','100%','100%','218px']}` (+ matching `flexBasis`/`flexShrink`/`flexGrow`/`paddingX`), cited against *"PDP hero content column, node 40000307:14476."*
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:951-953,1157` — the whole hero section pulled out of `PageContainer`'s uniform page-level containment (full-bleed + negative-margin cancellation of the sitewide `#app-main` padding) specifically to hand spacing control to the values above.

I distinguish this from two genuinely defensible bug fixes that I do **not** flag: `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts:228-235` (`zimmAppMain`'s `width: '100%'`) and `overrides/app/components/pageContainer/index.tsx:26-30` (`width: 'auto'` vs `'100%'`) — both are real, narrow, one-property fixes to a pre-existing `#app-main`-collapses-to-0-width bug that would otherwise block the gallery from rendering at all. A gallery with `flex={1}` doesn't need its sibling pinned to exactly 218px or the outer wrapper padded to exactly 140/40 to render — those precise, Figma-hero-frame-matched values only serve pixel-parity with SFCC-723's own frame, not "the gallery doesn't collapse." This is implemented ahead of, and independent of, SFCC-723's own confirmation state.

### Finding 2 — UNDER-delivery: pinch-to-zoom (PRD-061) — HIGH confidence

`.docs/prd/pdp.md:178` — **PRD-061 (confirmed):** *"Pinch-to-zoom and swipe-to-advance gallery navigation — mobile and touch."* Swipe-to-advance is delivered (native scroll-snap in `ZimmProductGallery`'s compact carousel). Pinch-to-zoom is not implemented anywhere in `zimmProductGallery/` or `zimmGalleryOverlay/` — no gesture handling of any kind — and it is not flagged anywhere as a deliberate, deferred gap (no doc comment, no story, no test), unlike this codebase's normal practice of recording known gaps explicitly. This item is also named verbatim in Jasmijn's 2026-09-04 comment as one of the SFCC-187 ACs that moved into SFCC-731 alongside the rest of the overlay work the PR did build. Since the PR built everything else on that list (open/close, thumbnail nav, scroll-to-navigate, focus/scroll restore), silently dropping this one item is a real, named gap, not an out-of-scope call the story text supports.

### Finding 3 — Colour-variant copy overreaches its own sanctioning comment — MEDIUM-HIGH confidence

Jasmijn's comment resolved the "still pending business examples" question by instructing the team to make the overlay's colour treatment *"consistent with the default gallery state."* `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:205-224` does this correctly for the single-colour case (`"Colour: <name>"`, matching the main PDP). For 2+ colours, it introduces a **new** Contentful uiCopy key, `pdp.gallery_overlay.colourLabel` (default `"Also available in"`, line 223), deliberately diverging from the PDP's own `"Colour:"` pattern — reasoned in the code's own comment (lines 212-214) as *"a field vs. alternatives"* distinction the PR authors invented themselves, not something sourced from business examples. This is new, unapproved copy in exactly the spot the BA comment flagged as still open.

### Finding 4 — Minor drive-by, low severity

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:922-926` — the `<h1 srOnly>` fallback text changed from the generic `"Product Details"` message to `product?.name`. <result>## PR #81 Review — Failure Modes, Graceful Degradation, Security, Accessibility

**1. Image error/fallback handling — `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:82-90`**

`alt` is derived from `item.kind === 'photo' ? item.alt : item.posterAlt`, and both `ZimmGalleryPhotoItem.alt`/`ZimmGalleryVideoItem.posterAlt` (lines 21-38) are non-optional `string` — never `string | undefined` at the type level. Traced the only production constructor, `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.ts:24` (`alt: image.alt ?? ''`), which coalesces SFCC's own optional `alt?: string` field, so a genuinely `undefined`/`null` `alt` cannot reach this component today (grepped for every `kind: 'photo'|'video'` construction in production code — only this one call site exists; the rest are stories/tests).

Given that, `aria-hidden={alt === '' || undefined}`: non-empty `alt` → `false || undefined` → `undefined` → React omits the attribute → the `role="img"` fallback stays in the accessibility tree, announced with `aria-label`. Empty `alt` → `true` → `aria-hidden="true"` → correctly removed from the a11y tree. This isn't just a static trace — the PR's own passing test (`index.test.tsx:58-66`) fires a real `error` event and asserts `getByRole('img', {name: 'Photo 1'})` is found afterward, which only passes if `aria-hidden` is correctly absent for non-empty alt. The fallback pattern itself (div, `role="img"`, `aria-label`, no visual content but a neutral fill) is a deliberate, reasonable choice — it gives AT users accessible-name parity with what a real `<img alt="...">` already provides even when broken (browsers keep exposing `alt` as the accessible name on 404), while giving sighted users a neutral box instead of the broken-image glyph. Not a gap.
CONFIRMED clean. 🔵. UNIFORM.

*Related finding, same theme, adjacent file:* `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:243-251` — the thumbnail-strip `<Image>` has **no `onError` handler at all**, unlike both of `ZimmMediaTile`'s branches. A failed thumbnail load in the expanded overlay renders the browser's raw broken-image icon with no fallback, breaking the "no broken-image icon" guarantee (AC 21) the rest of this PR was carefully built around. `alt=""` means no AT-facing regression, but it's a real, unguarded visual failure mode.
CONFIRMED. 🟡. ONE-OFF (every other image path in this PR wires `onError`; only this one doesn't).

**2. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sweep**

`grep -rn "dangerouslySetInnerHTML" overrides/` returns exactly one hit, in `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx:6` — a comment explaining that file *deliberately does not* use it. That file isn't in this PR's diff at all (confirmed via `git diff --stat` against `develop`). Zero occurrences anywhere in the 34 changed files.
CONFIRMED clean. 🔵. UNIFORM.

**3. `useUiCopy` missing/loading handling — `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:93,223`**

Traced the full chain, not just the hook: `useUiCopy.ts:52` (`useContext(UiCopyContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`) degrades to fallback text with no Provider. With a Provider mounted, `uiCopyProvider/index.tsx:21-37` builds `copyMap` from `(data ?? [])` and `t()` resolves `copyMap.get(key) ?? fallback` — explicitly documented as "fallback-on-failure by design, not just a loading placeholder." Went one hop further into `useContentful.ts`'s `useContentfulEntries` (the actual fetch): every failure path (missing config, non-ok response, thrown error, abort) is caught inside a `useEffect`/try-catch and converted to `setError(...)`, `data` stays at its initial `null` — no synchronous throw during render is possible anywhere in this chain. The PR's own test (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx:193-205`) exercises this exact call site with no `UiCopyProvider` wrapper and asserts the literal `'Also available in'` fallback renders.
CONFIRMED clean. 🔵. UNIFORM.

## Item 1 — Is the circle-variant/appendColon work purely additive?

**Core additive claim: CONFIRMED CLEAN.**
- `ZimmColourSwatch` (`.../atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:81`): `variant = 'square'` default. `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`'s square branch (lines 46–84, the `return` after the `if (variant === 'circle')` block at line 11) is byte-identical in every property/value to the pre-PR base file (base lines 3–44) — same order, same tokens. - `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` (`.../molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:78,80`): `appendColon = true` default. `labelText = label != null ? (appendColon ? \`${label}:\` : label) : ...` reduces to base's `label != null ? \`${label}:\` : ...` exactly when `appendColon` is true. The new `{appendColon && selectedName && (...)}` guard (line 179) reduces to base's `{selectedName && (...)}` exactly under the same default. Confirmed via full diff — no other lines in this file's rendering logic changed except passing `variant` through to `ZimmColourSwatch` (line 247) and to `useMultiStyleConfig` (line 167).

**Real finding — the chevron `boxSize` addition is NOT additive; it's a genuine, unconditional change to already-shipped UI.**

- **Exact before/after:**
  - Base `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:174`: `<ChevronLeftIcon aria-hidden />`
  - Base `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:183`: `<ChevronRightIcon aria-hidden />`
  - Head `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:193`: `<ChevronLeftIcon aria-hidden boxSize="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />`
  - Head `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:202`: `<ChevronRightIcon aria-hidden boxSize="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />`
  - This sits directly in the shared JSX rendered for both variants — **not** gated behind `variant === 'circle'`.

- **Magnitude, traced (not guessed):** `ChevronLeftIcon`/`ChevronRightIcon` are `createIcon()`-built Chakra icons (`overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx:108-118`). Chakra's own `Icon` component (`node_modules/@chakra-ui/icon/dist/icon.js`) calls `useStyleConfig('Icon', props)` and spreads the result **last**, i.e. it outranks the hardcoded `w:'1em',h:'1em'` default. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`'s base theme registers `Icon: { baseStyle: { boxSize: 6 } }` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/theme/components/base/icon.js`). Zimmermann's `theme/components/index.ts` registers no `Icon` override, and `theme/index.ts` only overrides `theme.space`, not `theme.sizes` (confirmed by that file's own comment: "sizes  Chakra sizes.lg=32rem vs iconSizes.lg=20px" — i.e. deliberately untouched). So **pre-PR, absent an explicit size prop, these icons rendered at Chakra's default `boxSize: 6` = 1.5rem = 24px.** An explicit `boxSize` prop at the JSX call site outranks `__css`/theme-baseStyle values in Chakra's precedence rules, so **post-PR they render at an explicit 16px** (`var(--zimm-scale-m)` = 1rem). Net: an unconditional ~33% shrink to the already-shipped, square-variant, main-PDP pagination chevrons.

- **Is it acknowledged?** Yes, in commit `8e0e50c`'s message: *"Reserved-width/gap math and pagination-chevron sizing in zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts made variant-aware **and corrected** against the Design System 2026 file's own 'ColourOptions' component (node 40001992:51882) — 4-per-page, 12px gap, **16px chevron icons in a 24px button**..."* — explicitly framed as a Figma-backed correction, not silent. It's also consistent with a comment that already existed **pre-PR** in `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts`'s `pageButton` part (base lines 156–157): *"...with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it..."* — i.e. the 16px intent was already documented, just never wired into the JSX until now.
- **But:** it is not gated by variant, and the PR's own top-level body (`gh pr view 81`) describes only the `ZimmProductGallery`/hero-layout work — it never mentions the circle variant, `appendColon`, or `ZimmGalleryOverlay` at all, and even states *"The gallery's own lightbox overlay is a separate component (SFCC-187), explicitly out of scope for SFCC-731"* — directly superseded by the later `8e0e50c` commit that adds exactly that overlay in the same PR. This looks like a stale PR description rather than concealment, but it means a reviewer relying on the PR body alone would have zero visibility into this change touching existing shipped UI.

**CONFIRMED · 🟡 · UNIFORM** (applies identically regardless of variant — not edge-case-gated).

## Item 3 — The `offered` colour-filter predicate duplication

- `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:87`: `const offered = values.filter((v) => Boolean(v.imageUrl) && v.orderable !== false);`
- `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:215`: `const offeredColourCount = (colourValues ?? []).filter((v) => Boolean(v.imageUrl) && v.orderable !== false).length;`

[]` prefix in the overlay is just a null-guard since `colourValues` is optional there vs. required `values` in the group). `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` (unchanged by this PR, confirmed identical on both sides of the diff) exports only `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` — no shared predicate exists anywhere for either file to reuse, despite the exact same shared-module precedent already being established for `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` (its own doc comment cites `footerShared.ts` as the model for "don't retype the same value twice"). ## Item 4 — Does the gallery overlay's colour set match product-detail's construction "exactly"?

**Structural claim: CONFIRMED true.** Both constructions combine natural variation values with SFCC-708 related swatches via the **identical** shared call:
```ts
buildRelatedSwatches((product?.c_relatedSwatches ?? []) as RelatedSwatch[], productUrlBuilder, SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID)
```
— `product-view/index.tsx:397-401` vs `product-detail/index.tsx:1074-1078`, textually identical arguments, only the destination variable name differs (`relatedColourValues` vs `relatedSwatches`). The related-swatch half of the colour set is 100% identical for both consumers, and `SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID` is a single constant imported by product-detail from product-view (not two independently-defined values).

**Field-by-field for the natural (non-related) values, `product-view/index.tsx:386-395` vs `product-detail/index.tsx:1060-1066`:**

| Field | product-detail | product-view | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `v.value ?? ''` | `v.value ?? ''` | identical |
| `name` | `v.name ?? v.value ?? ''` | `v.name` (no fallback) | **DIFFERENT — confirmed** |
| `imageUrl` | `v.image?.disBaseLink \|\| v.image?.link` (can be `undefined`) | `image?.disBaseLink \|\| image?.link \|\| ''` (defaults `''`) | textually different, **functionally equivalent — confirmed true equivalence, not a false one** |
| `href` | `v.href ?? undefined` | `v.href` | textually different, functionally identical (`ZimmColourSwatchValue.href?: string` is optional either way; `?? undefined` is a no-op) |
| `orderable` | `v.orderable ?? true` | `v.orderable ?? true` | identical |

**The `name` discrepancy is real and traces to a pre-existing type inconsistency, not a fresh typo:**
- `product-detail/index.tsx:184-190`'s own local type `SfccSwatchAttrValue` declares `name?: string` — optional — which is *why* its mapping defensively chains `v.name ?? v.value ?? ''`.
- `product-view/index.tsx:115` (pre-existing, **unchanged by this PR** — confirmed present verbatim in base at line 97) declares `type SfccVariationValue = { href?: string; name: string; ... }` — `name` **required**. This is describing the same underlying SFCC variation-value shape but disagrees with product-detail's own type for it. This PR's new `naturalColourValues` map (`product-view/index.tsx:387-395`) simply trusts this pre-existing, non-optional type and uses `v.name` raw.
- This flows into `ZimmColourSwatchValue.name: string` (required, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:22`) with no further guard, then into `ZimmColourSwatch`'s `aria-label={name}` (three call sites: `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:116,142,161`), whose own JSDoc states: *"Colour display name. Not rendered as visible text — used as the accessible name (`aria-label`)."* If `name` is ever genuinely `undefined` at runtime, React omits the `aria-label` attribute entirely — that swatch would have **no accessible name at all** (WCAG 4.1.2).

That said, `product-detail.tsx`'s separate, more-defensive type for the identical data (written specifically for feeding `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, the same consuming component) is itself evidence that whoever wrote that code already had reason to believe `name` can be absent for this exact shape — otherwise there'd be no reason to type it optional there. Given this project spans 8 storefronts and 11 locales, a variation value missing a localized display name is a realistic (if not routine) edge case, not a purely theoretical one.
- **No test anywhere exercises this**: `overrides/app/components/product-view/` has no `index.test.tsx` at all (only `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.test.ts`, unrelated). `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx`'s colour-selector tests (`:187-233`) pass pre-built literal `colourValues` objects directly to `ZimmGalleryOverlay` — they never exercise `product-view`'s actual mapping logic, so this gap wouldn't be caught by anything currently in the suite.

**CONFIRMED · 🟡 · ONE-OFF** (specific to the `name` field in the natural-values mapping only; `imageUrl`/`href`/`value`/`orderable` and the entire related-swatches half are all confirmed equivalent or identical).

## Item 5 — Test coverage for the circle variant

- **`ZimmColourSwatch` (atom)**: `index.test.tsx` and `index.stories.tsx` were **not touched by this PR at all** (absent from the diff stat), and contain zero mentions of `variant` or `circle`. The new prop and its entire CSS branch have **no test or story coverage whatsoever** at the atom level.
